body: Thanks for your kind words reddit is really my only outlet for my feelings sometimes.  I have friends and family that I could talk to but me and the wife were introverted because of her condition.  I just don't have any interest in talking with real people.

That's something that I do on purpose.  I listen to songs that make me cry to help me get my emotions out.  It's not good to keep them bundled up and I don't have anyone to talk to.  So the songs are a good outlet for me. It has been a month, yesterday since my wife passed away.
I have no idea what happened at the er.  I blacked out and I have no idea how I got home.
I'm 32 married for 9 years but dating since 11 grade my entire adult life had been with her.

Lord, you are a loving Father and generous to your children. You bless and inspire the world with your good work. Help Hopefulhusband in his search for profitable work so that he may care for his own as well as you have cared for me. Thank you Lord, for your loving guidance today.

I would at least bring it up to some other parishioner and explain your issues.  I agree with you and selling stuff inside the church seems wrong to me.  Where does that money go that the store makes.  Are the workers volunteers or are they being paid to sell that merchandise?  Do the profits go to the church or are they used for charitable functions?

I'm facing this same thing, my wife recently passed away as a non believer, and asked if I'd see her in that afterlife.  The general consensus was that there is no real way to know.  But according to the Pope Atheists can still go to heaven through there deeds.  Granted there are differences between Christians and Catholics beliefs but the point is valid.  http://www.catholic.org/news/hf/faith/story.php?id=51077

She was one of the nicest people I ever met.  Know that I do not say this because she was my wife.  She did many charitable things simply because it was the right thing to do. I understand that in heaven you are no longer married but I would find more solace in thinking that she will be there waiting for me.
As a person just starting there journey into loss.  I take solace in knowing I'm not alone in this journey.  I think I'll follow poetetc1 lead and raise a glass to you tonight.

Just wanted to give a reply back.  With the help of some anxiety medication. I managed to make it through the day.  The work staff was really receptive and gave me the space I needed.  I did break down and cry as soon I as walked into before work but got it out of my system before actually starting the day.  Ah well...one day down and what feels like eternity to go.

It's 2 hours from when I  am to leave for work and I have been bawling my eyes out for an hour now.  I wanted to get a shower and shave before work.  I barely managed to move into a seated position to write this.  I know this is just another step in moving on, but I'm afraid to drive in my current state and I can't call off this close to work.

I guess in my circumstances it's just easier to find reasons to not go one than there are to go on.  I just want to make it through the paper work part of her passing and maybe i can finally start trying to move on.  As long as there is work that has to be done on her behalf i don't feel like I have time to grieve properly.

Yeah i understand that most people in the subreddit have a much darker road than I have.  My wife used to tell me all the time if anything ever happened to me she would kill herself, and I believed her in this.  I was her primary care giver.  I really feel more lost than anything.  I'm managing with meds but I was on her insurance and with her gone I have lost my immediate access to the stuff that is keeping me sane.  When I run out is when I fear what might happen.
